headline: Bohm's two-out single in the 7th walks off Red Sox
recap: Alec Bohm lined a two-out, two-run single to left field in the bottom of the seventh, scoring J.T. Realmuto and Didi Gregorius and giving the Phillies a 6-5 win over the Red Sox in the opener of a seven-inning doubleheader. The hit came against Matt Barnes, who was charged with the blown save and the loss; Hector Neris earned the win after working around a leadoff walk and a single in the top of the inning.

Zach Eflin and Martin Perez both started and worked five innings. Eflin allowed three home runs, two to Rafael Devers and one to Alex Verdugo, and was charged with three earned runs on eight hits. Perez walked six and was charged with four runs, including a Gregorius solo homer in the second and a two-run single from Bohm in the third.

Devers went 3-for-4 with two home runs, a double and three RBI for Boston. His sixth-inning double, following a game-tying homer from Bobby Dalbec, put the Red Sox ahead 5-4 before Bohm's seventh-inning single reclaimed the lead for good.
